summary: 138 holdings; the top ten are 47% of the portfolio.
Trades a lot: about 93% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for 3.1 years.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 7 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Born in 1946; Wharton and Chicago. Ran high-yield and distressed-debt funds at Citicorp and TCW, then co-founded Oaktree in 1995. Brookfield bought 62% of Oaktree in 2019. Known for his memos to clients and books The Most Important Thing (2011) and Mastering the Market Cycle (2018).
profile.approach: Mostly credit: high-yield bonds, distressed debt and private equity, bought when others are forced to sell.
known: Raised $10.9 billion for distressed investments during the 2008 financial crisis, then the largest distressed debt fund.
profile.note: Oaktree is mainly a bond and private-credit investor; the 13F shows only the small part of its money held in US shares.
